title: Machine learning models to predict pathological complete response after chemoradiotherapy in muscle-invasive bladder cancer: toward optimized indications for bladder preservation

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Machine learning models to predict pathological complete response after chemoradiotherapy in muscle-invasive bladder cancer: toward optimized indications for bladder preservation》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Background and purpose · abstract-1-1】After bladder-sparing chemoradiotherapy (CRT) for muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC), residual microscopic disease may cause intravesical recurrence. This study aimed to develop machine learning models to predict pathological complete response (pCR) after CRT.

【Introduction · p0030】Radical cystectomy has long been the standard treatment for muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC), although it carries risks of perioperative complications and reduced quality of life related to urinary diversion. [1], [2] Multimodality bladder-preservation therapy based on chemoradiotherapy (CRT) is an alternative curative treatment. [3] Trimodality therapy, which consists of maximal transurethral resection of bladder tumor (TURBT) followed by CRT, is the most widely used bladder-preservation approach. [3] Previous studies have reported survival outcomes comparable to radical cystectomy in selected patients, and current guidelines include bladder preservation as a treatment option for appropriately selected patients. [4], [5], [6] However, primary resistance to CRT remains an important clinical problem. [7] Optimal patient selection remains difficult because most bladder-preservation studies include highly selected patients and usually assess CRT response with imaging and TURBT rather than complete surgical pathology. [8] Imaging and TURBT can miss microscopic residual cancer, which may later cause intravesical recurrence.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Machine learning models to predict pathological complete response after chemoradiotherapy in muscle-invasive bladder cancer: toward optimized indications for bladder preservation》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Patients · p0040】This study included patients with MIBC who were enrolled in one of two treatment protocols at our institution: the tetramodality bladder-preservation protocol or presurgical CRT before radical cystectomy. Both protocols included CRT followed by partial or radical cystectomy. [9], [12] Written informed consent was obtained from all patients before protocol enrollment. After institutional review board approval (approval number: M2019–192), we retrospectively reviewed 314 patients with cT2-4N0M0 bladder cancer who had pathologically confirmed urothelial carcinoma and received either protocol between 1997 and 2021. Twenty-nine patients (9.2%) did not undergo partial or radical cystectomy because of distant metastasis (n = 6, 1.9%) or patient withdrawal (n = 23, 7.3%) and were excluded. The final study cohort included 285 patients (91%) who underwent partial cystectomy (n = 148) or radical cystectomy (n = 137) after CRT. Fig. 1 shows patient inclusion. No formal sample size calculation was performed; all eligible patients treated during the study period were included.

【Patients · p0045】Patient and tumor characteristics and pathologic findings were obtained from medical records. Clinical stage was assigned according to the eighth edition of the TNM classification. [13] Staging included computed tomography of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis and magnetic resonance imaging of the bladder. Tumor size was defined as the maximum tumor diameter measured on pretreatment computed tomography or magnetic resonance imaging. For model development, tumor size was classified as >30 mm or ≤ 30 mm. Primary histologic grade was assessed in the pretreatment TURBT specimen using the 1999 WHO classification. Histologic variants and subtypes were assessed according to the 2016 WHO classification. [14], [15] Progression from prior non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) was defined as recurrence as MIBC after prior pathologically confirmed NMIBC had been treated before the current CRT course.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Machine learning models to predict pathological complete response after chemoradiotherapy in muscle-invasive bladder cancer: toward optimized indications for bladder preservation》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Conclusions · p0150】Using surgical pathology after CRT, we developed a machine learning model based on routinely available clinicopathologic variables to estimate pCR in MIBC. WeightedEnsemble_L4 had an AUC of 0.829 in the test cohort. In exploratory analyses, ≥cT3, tumor size >30 mm, concomitant CIS, and multiplicity were associated with lower pCR rates. Independent external validation is required to support future clinical implementation of the model to guide bladder-preservation treatment decisions.

【Results · abstract-3-1】Clinical T stages were T2/3/4 in 169/105/11 patients, respectively. Hydronephrosis was observed in 69 patients. Transurethral resection before CRT revealed multiplicity, BNI, and concomitant CIS in 108, 54, and 34 patients, respectively. Overall, 178/285 patients (62%) achieved pCR. WeightedEnsemble_L4 was selected as the final model and had a test-cohort AUC of 0.829 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.706-0.932). The calibration slope was 0.856 (95% CI, 0.469-1.639), and the wide CI indicated uncertainty in calibration.

【Statistical analysis · p0080】Continuous and categorical variables were compared with the Mann-Whitney U test and Fisher exact test, respectively. Metastasis-free survival and overall survival (OS) were calculated from the date of partial or radical cystectomy. Survival was estimated with the Kaplan-Meier method and compared with the log-rank test. All analyses other than machine learning were performed with JMP Pro version 17.0 (SAS Institute Inc., Cary, NC, USA) and R version 4.0.2 (R Foundation for Statistical Computing, Vienna, Austria). All tests were two-sided, and p < 0.05 was considered significant. We followed the TRIPOD statement for prediction model development and internal validation (Supplementary Table 1). Machine learning analyses used AutoGluon Tabular version 1.3.1 with Python version 3.11.13. There were no missing data for the predictors or the outcome.
